summary: Top Traders Unplugged weekly: October 2024 trend-following drawdown, Faber-style long-only trend overlay on SPY/TLT/EEM, and Brennan's outlier-hunting ensemble philosophy. Brennan argues for many uncorrelated systems with trailing stops and complex-adaptive-systems reasoning for why trends and fat tails exist.

coverage.note: intro, hurricanes, ensemble weather forecasting analogy
October 2024 CTA losses by sector, hidden correlations, dispersion
trend barometer, index performance, benchmark representativeness
replicator tracking error; listener question on SPY/TLT/EEM tactical allocation
Faber 10m SMA overlay, benefits and costs
overlay cons, regime bias in three-asset tests
Buffett diversification, outlier hunting, staggered ensemble entries
max concentration, margin cap, trailing stops
loose pants ensemble, drawdown improvement, eight core systems, reaction not prediction
complex adaptive systems, fractals, Holland signals/boundaries/emergence
stability, outliers as natural, Wolfram intro
nothing actionable: outro and sponsor read

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: these Ensemble models that they use for forecasting techniques are certainly better than what they used to be
claims.claim: Ensemble forecasting models beat older single-method forecasts, used as an analogy for ensembles of trend systems.

claims.speaker: Neils Kastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: fixed income has been the most difficult uh sector I think that Trend followers were just sort of settling into some long exposure over the summer after a few years riding the the short side of that market
claims.claim: Trend followers who had just flipped to long bonds after years short were hit when the market delivered a meaningful correction, making fixed income the worst sector in October 2024.
claims.direction: CTAs lose on bond-trend flips into corrections
claims.conditions: Right after a trend change into a new position
claims.testable: partly - needs CTA sector attribution data

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: subtly hidden beneath all of that Matrix of that very large diversification there hidden correlations and clearly everything sort of is reversing on us at the moment
claims.claim: Diversification across many markets can fail in a trend reversal because hidden correlations make many trends reverse together.
claims.conditions: In broad trend reversals diversification benefit shrinks
claims.testable: partly - measurable via correlation of trend-strategy P&L across sectors

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: I think dispersion is going to be one of the major topics that come out
claims.claim: Dispersion of results among trend followers is large in 2024, so benchmark indices do not describe individual managers.
claims.testable: yes - cross-sectional spread of manager returns

claims.speaker: Neils Kastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: it's certainly been very good at reflecting the challenges because it's down to 20 as of yesterday which is very low
claims.claim: A trend barometer (share of markets with a clear trend, short-horizon) reflects but does not predict how hard conditions are for trend followers; a reading near 14-20 is about the worst.
claims.indicator: Top Traders trend barometer (Neils's trend parameter)
claims.direction: low reading = hard for trend followers
claims.conditions: Uses a shorter horizon than traditional medium/long-term trend following
claims.testable: yes - level of barometer vs subsequent trend-following returns

claims.speaker: Neils Kastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: Bop 50 as a Wednesday was down 2.84% in October still up 1.23%
claims.claim: In October 2024 to mid-month BTOP50 was -2.84% (+1.23% YTD), SG CTA -3.64% (-1.22% YTD) and SG Trend almost -5% (-2.6% YTD), versus MSCI World -0.33% and S&P 500 flat.
claims.indicator: BTOP50, SG CTA, SG Trend, MSCI World, S&P 500 TR

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: the these indexes uh are dealing with uh the very large funds a bit like the the cap waiting we see in the S&P 500
claims.claim: CTA benchmark indices are weighted toward the largest funds, so a wider equal-ish index (Top Traders Unplugged index) shows less gloom and the big-fund index misrepresents the group.
claims.indicator: SG CTA, SG Trend vs Top Traders Unplugged index
claims.testable: yes - compare index construction and returns

claims.speaker: Neils Kastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: his product has massive tracking error this year luckily it's to the upside for him
claims.claim: A trend-replication product shows large tracking error versus the CTA benchmark in 2024 (to the upside).
claims.indicator: replicator tracking error vs CTA index

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: by investing in these uncorrelated ETFs we naturally obtain benefits of diversification that help to smooth the portfolio returns
claims.claim: Holding SPY, TLT and EEM (equities, long bonds, emerging markets) diversifies across weakly correlated asset classes and smooths returns, similar to all-weather portfolios.
claims.conditions: Depends on stock-bond correlation staying low

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: he used a simple long-term moving average often a 10mon simple moving average to determine whether to be in or out of each of those three asset classes
claims.claim: Faber-style tactical asset allocation: stay long an asset while price is above its 10-month simple moving average, otherwise move to cash or short bonds.
claims.direction: long when price above 10m SMA, else cash
claims.testable: yes - simple rule, long public history

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: the main goal here is downside protection
claims.claim: A long-only moving-average overlay limits large drawdowns by exiting assets in prolonged downtrends.
claims.conditions: Works only for prolonged declines, not sharp short crashes

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: these strategies tend to lag in their re-entry after a sudden Market bounce
claims.claim: The cost of the moving-average overlay is lag in re-entering after sharp quick recoveries, sacrificing upside.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: if you wanted um pure um short-term protection you would typically go into TI risk protection strategies like options
claims.claim: A trend-following overlay is slow risk mitigation, not an immediate hedge; options are the tool for short-term tail protection.
claims.testable: partly - compare overlay vs options hedge in short crashes

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: when you for instance out of the Spy you might uh be still in the the the TLT and you might still be in the eem
claims.claim: Applying the trend filter separately to several uncorrelated asset classes lets the portfolio rotate dynamically toward whichever asset is trending.
claims.direction: hold the assets that are above their moving average

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: you can enter these awful periods of whipsaw risk for instance when uh you're sort of going in and out of that simple moving average
claims.claim: In sideways markets a moving-average filter produces repeated in-and-out whipsaw losses.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: the long only constraint is another con from my perspective in that you can't participate in the downside move
claims.claim: A long-only trend filter forgoes profit from downtrends, and long-short trend following gives extra correlation benefits at portfolio level.

claims.speaker: Neils Kastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: you may not see the result for another 10 or 15 or 20 years
claims.claim: The benefit of a protective rule like a trend overlay may take 10-20 years to show, so discipline and a good starting date matter.

claims.speaker: Neils Kastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: if you only look at three instruments like that you may obviously be prone to the fact that they may have been in a specific regime
claims.claim: A backtest on three instruments risks regime bias, e.g. bonds had falling rates for about 37 of the past 40 years, so a bond trend result may not repeat; prefer broader diversification.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: diversification is protection against ignorance
claims.claim: Buffett's remark applies to outlier hunters: they diversify widely not to reduce risk but because they do not know where outliers will appear.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: our goal is to capture those rare but massive price moves called outliers
claims.claim: Trend following earns its profit from rare, massive outlier moves in the tails, while noise dominates most of the return distribution.
claims.testable: yes - decompose trend returns by tail events

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: we progressively concentrate our Capital into those Trends as outliers emerge
claims.claim: Start with small bets and concentrate capital progressively as a trend persists, so capital stays mostly inactive during noise.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: we're trying to avoid investing all of our Capital At Once into one Trend that may or may not unfold into an outli
claims.claim: Staggered activation of multiple uncorrelated entry systems (Donchian, Keltner, Bollinger breakouts) builds position size only as a trend endures.
claims.indicator: Donchian, Keltner and Bollinger channel breakouts

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: they all follow what they call a cpto kurtic signature with these big fat tails
claims.claim: All liquid markets show fat-tailed (leptokurtic) daily returns, with mean-reverting noise in the bulk and trending behaviour in the tails.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: this is why I refer to our approach as being nonlinearity squared
claims.claim: Each system in an ensemble captures the nonlinear price move, so an ensemble of 20 systems multiplies the payoff from outliers.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: diversifying for the specific purpose of being able to focus its capital towards what we call the events that matter
claims.claim: Diversify broadly to find the markets in outlier trends, then concentrate risk there.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: my knowledge of Serial correlation which is driving these nonlinear events through this amplification process this positive feedback process
claims.claim: Serial correlation from positive feedback drives outlier trends.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: I'm capping out at 20 at the moment simply because its margin the margin on these instruments
claims.claim: The number of ensemble systems is limited in practice by futures margin when risk concentrates in expensive-margin markets (e.g. palladium).

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: outliers naturally destroy correlations in markets
claims.claim: During outlier moves correlations between markets break down, so uncorrelated systems riding the outlier improve results.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: we must with each of our uncorrelated systems have trailing stops behind them at all times
claims.claim: Every system in the ensemble uses a trailing stop so open profits are not given back.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: with an ensemble of 20 uncorrelated markets the sum total of those being applied to the outlier actually does have very loose pants
claims.claim: An ensemble of many systems with individually tighter stops gives an aggregate looser trailing exit than two systems with wide stops.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: the draw down because of the uncorrelated Ensemble is always improving as I'm putting more and more uncorrelated
claims.claim: Adding more uncorrelated systems continuously improves drawdown and gives a small, diminishing MAR/CAGR increase with no sharp stopping point.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: we actually have eight core systems so the eight core systems but the variations in that are our parameter are variations as well
claims.claim: Most trend followers use few core approaches (about 5-10) with many parameter variations rather than 20 truly different systems.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: this nonpredictive philosophical approach which is basically reacting to Market moves it's not predicting it's reacting to them
claims.claim: Trend following reacts to price moves and does not forecast them.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: they build from seeds or kernels and then um in a scale invariant way as they progressively evolve
claims.claim: Markets behave like complex adaptive systems with fractal, scale-invariant structure that grow from small seeds into large trends, so no part is independent of the others.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: at the core of these complex adaptive systems are these three processes signals boundaries and emergent processes
claims.claim: Holland's framework for markets: signals, boundaries and emergence.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: these signals are not just simple data points but more importantly they interpretations of that information by the agent
claims.claim: Agents interpret the same signal differently, so reactions to signals vary and keep evolving.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: in financial markets boundaries take the form of for instance risk management rules regulatory Frameworks and system parameters
claims.claim: Boundaries such as risk rules and regulation limit the degrees of freedom of agents; a trend strategy has position limits, stops and leverage caps.
claims.indicator: position size limits, stop-loss, leverage caps

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: this is not a a stochastic state space where anything is possible like a random move
claims.claim: Boundaries make the price path constrained and path-dependent rather than random.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: they're not constrained by these time ordered constraints or spatial constraints there's no sense of path
claims.claim: Stochastic (ergodic) models of markets lack path dependence, whereas real markets show path dependence.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: enduring Trends is caused through positive feedback amplification nonlinear amplification
claims.claim: Enduring trends come from positive feedback loops with serial dependence, which trend followers exploit.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: a mean reverter or a convergent Trader negative feedback loops what they're doing is that they are explicitly going against the trend
claims.claim: Mean-reversion traders create negative feedback that interferes with trends, and this balance stabilises markets.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: we can't obviously all be Trend followers as the system would explode with positive feedback
claims.claim: Trend following is capacity-limited by the need for counterparties who trade against the trend.
claims.conditions: If too many follow trends, markets destabilise

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: to be expected much more frequently than what these traditional stochastic models would have you believe
claims.claim: Outliers are natural and occur more often than normal-distribution models imply.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: the ability to predict into the future is is limited or impossible because of these strange attractors
claims.claim: Nonlinear deterministic dynamics limit prediction, which supports reacting rather than predicting.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: they would need a computer that lasted the length of this universe to iterate in such a way to be able to predict what the system is going to do next
claims.claim: Complex systems are computationally irreducible, hence inherently unpredictable for any embedded observer.
